source.title: The dysphoric component of stress is encoded by activation of the dynorphin kappa-opioid system

confidence_rationale: Rigorous, multi-pronged primary study (KOR antagonism, dynorphin gene deletion, CRF/urocortin challenge, CRF-receptor-subtype antagonists, phospho-KOR immunolabelling) establishing that the dysphoric/aversive component of stress is specifically encoded by CRF2-driven dynorphin release acting on KOR, with KOR activation localised to amygdala, nucleus accumbens, dorsal raphe and hippocampus. Foundational grounding for treating kappa/dynorphin as the aversive-state substrate the layer builds the commitment-entropy axis on. Confidence held below 0.8 because the bridge from 'encodes dysphoria/aversion' to REE's 'commitment-entropy destabiliser' is an interpretive construct, and the data are rodent place-aversion / immobility, not commitment dynamics.
failure_signatures: The system encodes the aversive/dysphoric VALENCE of stress (place aversion, immobility); it is not shown to raise policy-competition entropy or destabilise commitments -- the 'commitment-entropy' reading is REE's overlay on an aversive-valence finding.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Aversive (place-aversion, immobility) effects of repeated forced-swim and inescapable-footshock stress, and of CRF/urocortin challenge, are blocked by KOR antagonism and absent in dynorphin-knockout mice; CRF-induced aversion is mediated by CRF2 (not CRF1) receptors driving dynorphin release and KOR activation; phospho-selective KOR antibody shows dynorphin-dependent KOR activation in basolateral amygdala, nucleus accumbens, dorsal raphe and hippocampus.
mapping.ree_translation: The layer (Section 3C / PHARM-018) reads mu/kappa as opposing poles on a commitment-entropy axis -- mu stabilises selected commitments (MECH-048), kappa destabilises and carries dysphoric/aversive state. Land et al. ground the kappa half: dynorphin/KOR is the dedicated substrate that encodes the aversive/dysphoric state, the 'aversive attractor wins by default' condition the layer maps to pathological kappa-driven destabilisation. The hippocampal/amygdalar KOR activation also ties it to the terrain and harm planes (MECH-088).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The finding is about aversive VALENCE encoding, not about commitment dynamics or policy entropy. Mapping kappa-dysphoria onto a 'commitment-entropy destabiliser' is REE's construct and is not tested here. Rodent stress-aversion assays; mu-opioid (the proposed stabiliser pole, MECH-048) is not examined in this paper.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; conditioned place aversion / forced-swim immobility + genetic and pharmacological dissection + phospho-KOR immunohistochemistry.

confidence_components.notes: Landmark primary study, multi-method, strong causal controls. Mapping_fidelity moderate: cleanly grounds kappa/dynorphin as the aversive-state substrate, but the commitment-entropy construct is an REE overlay. Transfer risk moderate (rodent stress assays -> human affective state).
